_metadata.description: P1 requirements — records absorption, run linkage, operator surfaces, and the multi-space embedding refinement. All planned; validation entries declare intended evidence without asserting refs that do not exist.

requirements.title: Work-record memory kind
requirements.description: A work-record memory kind carries the fields the swarm-manager records contract defined — trigger, approach, evidence, outcome — validated as a required set at write. This replaces `swarm-manager records create` as the agent-facing verb so agents learn one write surface. Backlog association is derived from run correlation rather than a hand-passed flag, which is the failure this absorption is designed to fix.

validation.notes: A work-record note missing a required field is rejected with a field-specific error.
A work-record written inside a run resolves its backlog association from correlation with no flag passed.
Migration review: existing swarm-manager records import as work-record memories with narrative and outcome preserved.

requirements.title: Run correlation and sibling events
requirements.description: A memory written inside an agent run stores the receipt correlation emitted automatically by api-core — run id, workflow execution id, actor kind. Retrieval exposes a command that lists the other events from that run. Memory stores identifiers only and never a denormalized copy of run data, so there is exactly one truth about any run.

validation.notes: A write carrying run correlation persists the ids and no copied run payload.
A write with absent correlation (operator shell, null run id) succeeds and stores no correlation.
The sibling-events command resolves a stored run id to the other events of that run.

requirements.title: Tree descent
requirements.description: Zooming a summary renders that node's immediate constituents — leaves verbatim, child summaries as summaries labeled with their span and depth — and descent repeats to the leaves. A reader must never mistake a summary for an original, so every rendered summary is labeled as one.

validation.notes: Zoom on a depth-2 node returns its immediate children, not its transitive leaves.
Rendered summary nodes carry an explicit summary label with span and depth; leaves do not.

requirements.title: Supersession-aware summarization
requirements.description: When a candidate cluster contains contradicting entries, the summarization prompt resolves by recency rather than conjoining both claims. Because clustering is semantic, near-identical contradictions co-occur in the same cluster, so resolution is always a within-cluster judgment and never a corpus-wide contradiction search.

validation.notes: A cluster containing a claim and its later negation summarizes to the later claim only.
A cluster of compatible claims summarizes without dropping the distinct claims it can fit in budget.
Operator review of summarization output on a real cluster sample, distinguishing intended fact dropping from fact mutation.

requirements.title: Multi-space facet embedding
requirements.description: Several short derived texts per memory — topic, rule/implication, entities — are each embedded normally rather than conditioning one vector on an instruction. This yields multiple neighbourhoods per memory using the embedding model already deployed fleet-wide, and keeps the derived texts human-readable so bad clustering is debuggable. Embeddings intended for clustering use the model's clustering task prefix rather than the document prefix.

validation.notes: A memory produces one embedding per derived facet text, each retrievable and attributable to its source text.
Clustering-purpose embeddings request the clustering task prefix; retrieval-purpose embeddings request the document prefix.
Two memories related only on one facet co-cluster in that facet's space and not in the others.

requirements.title: Operator review surface
requirements.description: A UI for browsing the journal as a timeline, inspecting the frontier so the compaction staircase is legible, and correcting a memory's facet or pinned state. Correction is the operator's control over what the fleet believes; a misclassified standing rule is the highest-consequence error the system can make, so re-facet and pin/unpin are first-class actions rather than admin afterthoughts.

validation.notes: Journal timeline renders loading, empty, partial, and error states.
Frontier explorer distinguishes leaves from summaries and shows each summary's span and depth.
Re-facet and pin/unpin actions round-trip to the API and reflect in the rendered state.

requirements.title: Harness prompt-block install
requirements.description: A command installs and updates the prompt block that teaches each harness to call the memory CLI instead of writing its own store, targeting CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and equivalent runtime convention files. The block is idempotent and delimited so re-running updates in place rather than appending duplicates.

validation.notes: Installing twice leaves exactly one delimited block with the current content.
Installing into a file with unrelated content preserves that content outside the delimiters.
